replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: You’re right — Iceland did have much more woodland when the first Norse settlers arrived. Over the centuries, much of it disappeared because of clearing, grazing, and the harsh environment. People also relied on driftwood and imported timber for buildings and boats. It’s a fascinating part of Iceland’s history that often gets overlooked. Thank you for bringing it up, and thanks for watching! Wishing you a wonderful day! 🇮🇸

Very well done.

Jim Johnson
Central North Carolina 
USA
